_readme: Technical Product Marketing, Version 1.1: the rebuilt case study through 01 Hero, 02 Foundation, 03 the transitional statement, 04 Website and 05 Technical documentation, then Contact. Copy is John's approved wording from the V1 concept and the V1.1 brief (October 12, 2026); the chapter notes under the documentation walkthrough are drafted from the brief's confirmed facts and are open to John's edits. The foundation library lists twelve named documents in the brief's order, with display numbers 00 to 11 (not their Linear numbers); no document body is read, quoted or published.

hero.headline: Building the system behind the message.
hero.copy: I built the strategic foundation that turned Bolt Liquidity’s technical complexity into a clear market narrative, then carried it across documentation, web experiences, articles, and campaigns.

foundation._headline: Always two lines, broken where the brief breaks it.
headline: Before the message
came the foundation.
foundation.copy: Before Bolt Liquidity could be explained externally, it needed a shared internal language. I turned stakeholder interviews and product research into the positioning, claims, proof points, and narrative architecture that guided every public-facing expression.
foundation._documents: In the brief's order, from internal input through market understanding, strategic definition, governance and expression. Each document has its own muted accent (its strip and its faded icon) and its own icon; no two neighbors share a hue family. The interview count is not published.
foundation._depth: Unlabeled, neutral covers after the last named document: no number, title, subline or icon, only the suggestion that the library runs deeper.

statement.copy: The strategy did not stay in a document. It became the website, technical documentation, articles, campaigns, and content that brought the product to market.

website.title: Website
website._meta: Label and value pairs, in order. **Text** marks a name set in bold.

meta.label: Brief
value: Rebuild the website around Bolt Liquidity’s new product positioning.

meta.label: Role / Services
value: Web strategy, information architecture, copywriting, UX direction, conversion design, and design collaboration.

meta.label: Credits
value: Visual design, brand expression, front-end implementation, and deployment: **Bob van der Meer**. Bob handled typography, color, visual banners, implementation, and deployment while collaborating closely with John on the design, interactions, revisions, and final experience.

website.contribution: I translated Bolt Liquidity’s new positioning into the website’s complete structure and narrative: defining the section architecture, writing every line of copy, shaping key interactions and scroll behavior, and building the CTA and partnership-form flows. I partnered with Bob van der Meer through design revisions, implementation, and launch to deliver the full rebuild in two weeks.

documentation.title: Technical documentation

meta.label: Brief
value: Replace a fragmented, rudimentary GitBook with a complete documentation system aligned to Bolt Liquidity’s new positioning.

meta.label: Goal
value: Give technical and developer audiences a clear, connected path from product understanding to implementation while controlling which internal technical details could be communicated publicly.

meta.label: Role / Responsibilities
value: Platform research and selection, documentation strategy, information architecture, technical writing, MDX implementation, cross-referencing, CTA architecture, architecture-diagram direction, public-information governance, GitHub publishing, and collaboration across engineering, liquidity, and design.

meta.label: Credits
value: Visual design and interactive implementation: **Bob van der Meer**. Bob handled typography, color, branded visual treatments, custom effects, and the final implementation of the interactive architecture diagram in collaboration with John.
Technical review and validation: Bolt Liquidity engineering and liquidity teams.

documentation.contribution: I replaced a fragmented GitBook with a new Mintlify documentation system aligned to Bolt Liquidity’s repositioning. I owned the platform research, information architecture, cross-references, calls to action, technical writing, MDX implementation, and GitHub publishing. Working with engineering, liquidity, and design, I translated complex product architecture into a public-facing interactive experience, governed what could be disclosed, and wrote every layer of supporting explanation.
documentation._chapters: The three proof points of the edited walkthrough, with where each begins in it (seconds, at the middle of the cross-fade into it). The notes are drafted from the brief's confirmed facts.

chapters.title: Documentation home
chapters.note: One branded Mintlify system in place of scattered GitBook pages, organized from product understanding to implementation.

chapters.title: Architecture diagram
chapters.note: I developed the early diagram with engineering, validated it with the liquidity team, refined its structure, filtered out internal-only information, briefed design, and wrote every pop-up explanation. Final visual design and interactive implementation: Bob van der Meer.

chapters.title: Developer SDK
chapters.note: The existing SDK code was preserved while the surrounding structure, explanations, cross-references, navigation, and presentation were rebuilt.
